sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: German has two common ways to say no: nicht and kein.

blocks.text: Use nicht to negate a verb, an adjective or a whole statement: Ich arbeite nicht. Das ist nicht mein Schlüssel. Use kein before a noun that has ein or no article: Ich habe kein Geld.
Possessive articles work like ein: mein, dein, sein and ihr take the same endings. Before a feminine noun they add -e (meine Schwester), and before a plural noun they add -e as well (meine Bücher).

blocks.title: Quick decision
blocks.text: If the noun would use ein, negate it with kein. If you are negating anything else, use nicht.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Ich komme nicht. Das ist nicht teuer.
kein before a noun with ein

items: kein takes the same endings as ein: kein, keine, keinen.
Nicht usually goes near the end of the sentence, before an adjective or infinitive.
Mein and dein belong to the speaker and the person spoken to.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The ch is soft after i. Keep the vowel short.
Two syllables: MY-ne, with a clear final -e.

blocks.text: A bare "Nein" can sound abrupt in shops and offices. A short explanation softens it: "Nein, danke" or "Das habe ich leider nicht".
In Germany, directness is often valued, but politeness still matters. Adding "leider" (unfortunately) makes a refusal feel less personal.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: At the lost-property desk, Ben cannot find his key.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.de: Guten Tag, ich habe meinen Schlüssel verloren.
lines.en: Hello, I have lost my key.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.de: Nein, das ist nicht mein Schlüssel.
lines.en: No, that is not my key.

lines.speaker: Mitarbeiterin
lines.de: Kein Problem. Wir haben noch einen anderen.
lines.en: No problem. We have another one.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Nicht or kein?
sections.lede: Choose the negation that matches what you are saying no to.

rows: Negates a verb, adjective or statement: Ich schlafe nicht.
Negates a noun with ein or no article: Ich habe kein Auto.
Possessive before masculine or neuter nouns: mein Hund, dein Buch.
Possessive before feminine or plural nouns: meine Tasche, deine Bücher.

blocks.text: The negative article kein changes in the accusative just like ein: Ich habe keinen Hund.

sections.tip: Do not use "nicht ein". German says kein: Ich habe kein Geld, not Ich habe nicht ein Geld.

sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.

script.speaker: Herr Lang
script.de: Nein, leider nicht. Ist das Ihr Schlüssel?
script.en: No, unfortunately not. Is this your key?

script.de: Nein, das ist nicht mein Schlüssel.

questions.prompt: What is Frau Klein looking for?
questions.explanation: She asks about "meinen Schlüssel", her key.

questions.prompt: Does the key belong to her?
questions.explanation: She says "Das ist nicht mein Schlüssel", so it is not hers.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Say two things you do not have and one thing that is yours.

model.de: Ich habe kein Auto. Ich habe keine Zeit. Das ist mein Fahrrad.
model.en: I have no car. I have no time. That is my bicycle.

tips: Use kein before the noun and check its gender.
Use nicht when you negate a verb: Ich arbeite nicht.
Say the three sentences without stopping, then listen to the model.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.why: Zeit is a noun with no article, so negate it with keine.
German uses kein, not nicht ein.
Schwester is feminine, so mein needs the ending -e.
